report:
Freshly inspected the current claim, ordinary product_catalog association and its captured src/inspector.rs context, and the complete associated TODO test after review start with the current coordinator instructions. This assessment is based on present source, not the prior approval.

The requirements are positive availability; selection without requesting advertised products; returned opaque product IDs, labels and URLs; a shared local/external mechanism; and omission of unsupported products. selected_symbol constructs the local SelectedSymbol from directory metadata and invokes product_catalog only for a valid locator. The synthetic root has no locator and returns an empty catalog. product_catalog always lists identity, adds source when symbol_span exists, and adds concrete-ir/signature/diagnostics/typed-ir only when local_fn recognizes a local function. local_fn explicitly excludes external functions and other symbol kinds. symbol_span returns local spans, including generated-symbol spans, and no span for external/intrinsic symbols. source_product handles generated spans with a generated-source notice, so their source entry is supported rather than an unavailable page.

external_selected_symbol resolves canonical identity, then external_product_catalog emits identity for external symbols; signature only for Fn/Trait/Struct/Enum; and items only for Mod/Enum/Trait. All other match arms omit those capabilities. Both catalogs call product_descriptor, which returns producer-owned string IDs and human labels plus the same /api/v1/product URL form; percent_encode protects the symbol path including non-ASCII bytes and reserved URL characters. Opaque here means callers consume the supplied identifiers and URLs; availability is explicitly advertised rather than inferred by callers.

The catalog functions consult identity, kind and span metadata only. They do not call product execution, signature, body, source-text or reflection generation. symbol() uses selection and records a selection run; product() separately invokes identity_product. External path resolution walks owner membership and canonical identity without invoking external_product. Actual local signature/body/diagnostic/CST accesses and external signature/item product generation occur in the explicit identity_product/external_product branches, matching the positive catalog kind restrictions. Missing or unsupported product cases return None. Local and external catalogs therefore share descriptors and request mechanism despite differing supported sets.

The complete associated test set is sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_product_availability. Its empty body has no meaningful assertions and proves none of these properties. Its comment explicitly defers associating and reviewing local/external catalog tests that assert exact positive lists and forbid product-detail reads. This is accepted as a visible evidence deferral under the captured meta.reviews.decisions policy. Prerequisites for completing it are reviewed fixtures for local/external symbol kinds, explicit descriptor/list assertions including unsupported omissions and URLs, and observations that would detect an eager product request while selecting. For example, advertising typed-ir for an external function or calling function.sig while listing products would need detection; the current placeholder cannot detect either. No N/A entries or TODO implementation entries exist. This approval does not relabel deferred tests as completed coverage.

Only source review and review start/read/record commands were performed by this reviewer. Behavioral suites are centrally owned by the coordinator; no test pass is claimed here. Dependencies used for this judgment are in the automatically captured inspector file, with the review acceptance policy captured separately by review read. No source edits were made and no further edits are requested beyond the existing explicit coverage deferral.
